title: Stay Right Until You Pass
hook: Two lanes south. He's sitting in the left.
scene: Central Avenue, two lanes south, rain on a Kent morning. You are in the right. A primer sedan is doing twenty-eight in the left. A pickup is already using that left to get around him. The empty ahead of the sedan is not a place to sit. The schedule would love it anyway. The left is for passing, then coming back.
decision: The left has a slow sedan and a pickup passing him. Where do you put this bus?

options.text: Move left now and sit in the empty — through traffic can use either
options.result: You take the left and become the new slow. A pickup that was using that lane as a pass has to stand on it. Horn. The sedan never moved. You spent his margin so you could sit pretty.

options.text: Hold the right. Pass only if he stays slow and the left is clear
options.result: You stay right. He stays twenty-eight. When the left is empty and you need him, you take it, clear him, and come back. The pickup behind never has to lift. Through traffic stayed through.

options.text: Straddle both — the Ledger is wide enough that the sedan will yield
options.result: You occupy the dashed line. He brakes. The pickup goes for the shoulder. You own two lanes and nobody can pass you, including you.

options.text: Drop to twenty and wait for him to notice and move over
options.result: You become a rolling roadblock in the right. He never looks. The stack behind you grows. You taught Central that the Ledger is the problem.

debrief: When several lanes go the same way, keep right except to pass. You saved the left for the people who actually need it.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Keep right except to pass on a multi-lane road; the left is for passing, not cruising.
